item.title: IWIA Launches Indian Women Arbitrators Database to Bridge Gender Gap
item.description: Indian Women in International Arbitration (IWIA) has launched the Indian Women Arbitrators Database through tri-city events in Delhi, Mumbai and Bengaluru to address gender disparity in arbitrator appointments. The post IWIA Launches Indian Women Arbitrators Database to Bridge Gender Gap appeared first on SCC Times.

item.title: Call for Participation | 14th Justice V. M. Tarkunde National Parliamentary Debate
item.description: ILS Law College announces the 14th Justice V. M. Tarkunde National Parliamentary Debate 2026, a premier Asian Parliamentary debating tournament bringing together students from across India for three days of rigorous discourse and advocacy. item.title: Severe injuries and missing nails, teeth: Chhattisgarh HC takes suo motu cognizance of illegal tiger poaching in Revti Forest, seeks response from Principal Chief Conservator
item.description: “Such a method is not only fatal to animals but poses a grave and imminent danger to human life as well, as any unsuspecting person may come into contact with the live electric traps laid for illegal poaching.” The post Severe injuries and missing nails, teeth: Chhattisgarh HC takes suo motu cognizance of illegal tiger poaching in Revti Forest, seeks response from Principal Chief Conservator appeared first on SCC Times.

item.title: What prompted Supreme Court to direct day-to-day hearing in Ajmer Sharif blast case
item.description: The Court issued specific direction to the Trial Court to expedite the hearing… particularly when the petitioner is languishing under incarceration for more than 8½ years. The post What prompted Supreme Court to direct day-to-day hearing in Ajmer Sharif blast case appeared first on SCC Times.

item.title: Attorney-Client Privilege and the Constitutional State: Liberty’s Last Refuge in the Age of Surveillance
item.description: Attorney-client privilege is not a vestige of professional etiquette; it is the living spirit of constitutionalism. by Devadipta Das* The post Attorney-Client Privilege and the Constitutional State: Liberty’s Last Refuge in the Age of Surveillance appeared first on SCC Times.

item.title: Jharkhand HC: Special Auxiliary Police personnel are contractual appointees with a maximum tenure of 7 years, not entitled to superannuation benefit
item.description: “If any age of superannuation was to be included or read into the scheme, the same could only be done by a proper amendment and not by any recommendatory letter.” The post Jharkhand HC: Special Auxiliary Police personnel are contractual appointees with a maximum tenure of 7 years, not entitled to superannuation benefit appeared first on SCC Times.

item.title: Sneak Peek into the Latest Edition of Avtar Singh’s Law of Arbitration and Conciliation — Timeless Authority, Reimagined for Today by Saurabh Bindal
item.description: The 13th Edition of Avtar Singh’s Law of Arbitration and Conciliation is set to release soon, incorporating recent legislative developments, landmark judicial pronouncements, and evolving arbitral practice in India. The post Sneak Peek into the Latest Edition of Avtar Singh’s Law of Arbitration and Conciliation — Timeless Authority, Reimagined for Today by Saurabh Bindal appeared first on SCC Times.

item.title: Fox & Mandal Represents Karan Paul in Punjab Kings Ownership Arbitration
item.description: Fox & Mandal successfully represented Karan Paul before the Punjab & Haryana High Court in a high-profile arbitration concerning the Punjab Kings IPL franchise. The Court appointed Justice Harinder Singh Sidhu (Retd.) as sole arbitrator to adjudicate the chairmanship dispute in KPH Dream Cricket Private Limited, marking a key procedural milestone in the shareholder dispute. The post Fox & Mandal Represents Karan Paul in Punjab Kings Ownership Arbitration appeared first on SCC Times.

item.title: Deadline Extension for Call for Papers for the Fifth Volume of its annual publication, HPNLU Law Journal
item.description: HPNLU, Shimla has extended the deadline for submissions to the Fifth Volume of the HPNLU Law Journal, inviting interdisciplinary socio-legal manuscripts across multiple categories until February 15, 2026.
